## Proposed change
<!--

It appears `sensor.time` has had a bug that could cause an exception at startup if the first update happens before the `TimeDateSensor` object is fully initialized (specifically before `entity_id` is set.) It seems the recent changes that allow Home Assistant to startup more quickly have made this bug more likely to manifest itself.

The change postpones the first scheduled update until _after_ the `TimeDateSensor` object has been fully initialized.

issue_context.title: sensor.time not updating
issue_context.body:
## The problem
sensor.time gets stuck at a value and does not update. Intermittent, but when it does happen, it is immediately after a restart.

## Environment
- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.113.x
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.112.x
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Hassio on a rPi 3B+
- Integration causing this issue: time_date
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```
- platform: time_date
```

## Traceback/Error logs
```
2020-08-03 10:21:01 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant] Error doing job: Exception in callback HomeAssistant.async_run_job(<bound method... Time: 10:21>>, datetime.date... tzinfo=<UTC>))
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/events.py", line 81, in _run
    self._context.run(self._callback, *self._args)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/core.py", line 381, in async_run_job
    target(*args)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/time_date/sensor.py", line 139, in point_in_time_listener
    self.async_write_ha_state()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 286, in async_write_ha_state
    raise NoEntitySpecifiedError(
homeassistant.exceptions.NoEntitySpecifiedError: No entity id specified for entity Time
```

## Additional information

review_comments: Ah, nice! I wasn't aware of `async_on_remove`.

But wait. I don't think that will work. First, because `async_track_point_in_utc_time()` will effectively remove it itself when it runs the action. And second because `async_track_point_in_utc_time()` is also called in `self.point_in_time_listener()` every time the sensor updates. Using `async_on_remove` would constantly add to the list "un-subcribers" that become stale when the next is added.

BTW, due to these two points, that's why in `self.point_in_time_listener()` it overwrites `self.unsub`, because by the time it runs, the previously saved "un-subscribe" has effectively already run.
oh wait, yes you're right. Sorry. I was thinking of track interval.
